newsitem.title: RUSSIA: DeBakey sees Yeltsin in Kremlin in 2-3 weeks.
newsitem.headline: DeBakey sees Yeltsin in Kremlin in 2-3 weeks.

text.p: U.S. heart surgeon Michael DeBakey said on Thursday that Russian President Boris Yeltsin could be back at home in two to three weeks.

"I think he could go back to the Kremlin in two to three weeks," DeBakey said in an interview. But he added it would take several weeks longer before Yeltsin would be able to work at full strength, following Tuesday's quintuple heart bypass.

DeBakey, 88, said Yeltsin was walking in his hospital room on Thursday morning and would be able to move from the Cardiology Research Centre where he was operated on to the more comfortable Central Clinical Hospital on Friday.
DeBakey, a leading U.S. heart surgeon who advised on Yeltsin's surgery, said the president was recovering rapidly and would become a "new man".
"You're going to see a vigorous leader," he said.
DeBakey said Yeltsin was "pushing" doctors to leave the Cardiology Centre but that the 65-year-old president generally was not a difficult patient.
